subject: MATH
title: Mathematics 6
description: Grade 6 math moves from whole-number arithmetic toward algebraic thinking. Students reason with ratios, rates and percents, complete their understanding of division with fractions, extend the number system to negative rational numbers, write and solve one-variable equations, find area, surface area and volume, and begin statistics by describing distributions. The sequence follows the Illustrative Mathematics / Open Up Resources Grade 6 scope used by many California districts.
framework: California Common Core State Standards for Mathematics; 2023 CA Mathematics Framework

standards.6.RP.A.1: Understand the concept of a ratio and use ratio language to describe a relationship between two quantities.
standards.6.RP.A.2: Understand the concept of a unit rate a/b associated with a ratio a:b (b not 0) and use rate language.
standards.6.RP.A.3: Use ratio and rate reasoning (tables, tape diagrams, double number lines, equations) to solve real-world problems.
standards.6.RP.A.3a: Make tables of equivalent ratios, find missing values, plot pairs on the coordinate plane, and compare ratios.
standards.6.RP.A.3b: Solve unit rate problems, including unit pricing and constant speed.
standards.6.RP.A.3c: Find a percent of a quantity as a rate per 100; solve problems finding the whole given a part and the percent.
standards.6.RP.A.3d: Use ratio reasoning to convert measurement units; transform units when multiplying or dividing quantities.
standards.6.NS.A.1: Interpret and compute quotients of fractions and solve word problems involving division of fractions by fractions.
standards.6.NS.B.2: Fluently divide multi-digit numbers using the standard algorithm.
standards.6.NS.B.3: Fluently add, subtract, multiply and divide multi-digit decimals using standard algorithms.
standards.6.NS.B.4: Find the greatest common factor (to 100) and least common multiple (to 12); use the distributive property to factor sums.
standards.6.NS.C.5: Use positive and negative numbers to represent quantities in real-world contexts and explain the meaning of 0.
standards.6.NS.C.6: Understand a rational number as a point on the number line; extend number lines and coordinate axes to negative numbers.
standards.6.NS.C.6c: Find and position integers and other rational numbers on a number line and coordinate plane.
standards.6.NS.C.7: Understand ordering and absolute value of rational numbers.
standards.6.NS.C.8: Solve real-world problems by graphing points in all four quadrants, including distances between points sharing a coordinate.
standards.6.EE.A.1: Write and evaluate numerical expressions involving whole-number exponents.
standards.6.EE.A.2: Write, read and evaluate expressions in which letters stand for numbers.
standards.6.EE.A.2c: Evaluate expressions and formulas (e.g., V = s^3, A = 6s^2) at specific values using order of operations.
standards.6.EE.A.3: Apply the properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions.
standards.6.EE.A.4: Identify when two expressions are equivalent.
standards.6.EE.B.5: Understand solving an equation or inequality as finding which values make it true; use substitution to check.
standards.6.EE.B.6: Use variables to represent numbers and write expressions when solving real-world problems.
standards.6.EE.B.7: Solve real-world problems by writing and solving equations of the form x + p = q and px = q for nonnegative rational numbers.
standards.6.EE.B.8: Write inequalities of the form x > c or x < c for real-world constraints and represent solutions on number lines.
standards.6.EE.C.9: Use variables to represent two quantities that change together; relate dependent and independent variables with tables, graphs and equations.
standards.6.G.A.1: Find the area of right triangles, other triangles, special quadrilaterals and polygons by composing and decomposing shapes.
standards.6.G.A.2: Find the volume of right rectangular prisms with fractional edge lengths; apply V = lwh and V = bh.
standards.6.G.A.3: Draw polygons in the coordinate plane given vertices; use coordinates to find side lengths.
standards.6.G.A.4: Represent three-dimensional figures using nets of rectangles and triangles and use nets to find surface area.
standards.6.SP.A.1: Recognize a statistical question as one that anticipates variability in the data.
standards.6.SP.A.2: Understand that a data distribution can be described by its center, spread and overall shape.
standards.6.SP.A.3: Recognize that a measure of center summarizes all values with one number, while a measure of variation describes how values vary.
standards.6.SP.B.4: Display numerical data in plots on a number line, including dot plots, histograms and box plots.
standards.6.SP.B.5: Summarize numerical data sets in relation to their context (count, attribute measured, center and variability, shape, outliers).
standards.MP.1: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
standards.MP.3: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

units.title: Area and Surface Area
units.big_idea: Area can be found by cutting, rearranging and decomposing shapes; surface area is the total area of a solid's faces.

units.title: Introducing Ratios
units.big_idea: A ratio compares two quantities, and equivalent ratios describe the same relationship at different scales.

units.title: Unit Rates and Percentages
units.big_idea: Unit rates and percents (rates per 100) let us compare and convert quantities efficiently.

units.title: Dividing Fractions
units.big_idea: Division asks 'how many groups?' or 'how much in each group?', and those questions work for fractions too.

units.title: Arithmetic in Base Ten
units.big_idea: Place value makes the standard algorithms for decimals and long division work.

units.title: Expressions and Equations
units.big_idea: Variables let us write general relationships, find unknowns and show how one quantity depends on another.

units.title: Rational Numbers
units.big_idea: Negative numbers extend the number line and the coordinate plane to describe opposite directions and values below zero.

units.title: Data Sets and Distributions
units.big_idea: Statistical questions expect variability; we describe a distribution by its center, spread and shape.

units.title: Putting It All Together
units.big_idea: The year's tools combine to model real situations.

objectives: Find area by decomposing and rearranging
Derive and use A = bh for parallelograms

days.title: Tiling the plane
days.work: Compare areas of tangram shapes by covering them with smaller pieces, then explain in writing why two different-looking shapes can have equal area.

days.title: Composing and decomposing
days.work: Find the area of L-shaped and staircase regions on graph paper three different ways (cut apart, enclose and subtract, rearrange) and record each method.

days.title: Parallelograms to rectangles
days.work: Cut a paper parallelogram along its height, slide the triangle to form a rectangle, and use this to write A = b x h; solve 8 parallelogram area problems.

days.title: Bases and heights
days.work: Identify every base-height pair on tilted parallelograms, including heights that fall outside the shape, and compute areas of 10 drawn figures.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a 10-problem quiz on rectangle and parallelogram area and write one sentence correcting any error you made.

weeks.assessment: Quiz: area of composite rectangles and parallelograms; explanation of why A = bh works.

objectives: Derive A = 1/2 bh from two copies of a triangle
Find any base and height of a triangle

days.title: Two copies make a parallelogram
days.work: Trace and cut two identical triangles, join them into a parallelogram, and explain why a triangle's area is half of b x h.

days.title: Right triangles
days.work: Find areas of 10 right triangles on a grid and write a rule using the two legs as base and height.

days.title: Any base, any height
days.work: For acute and obtuse triangles, draw all three heights with a ruler and show the area comes out the same using each base.

days.title: Triangle formula practice
days.work: Solve 12 triangle-area problems including missing-base and missing-height problems (e.g., area 24 sq cm and base 8 cm; find height).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a quiz mixing triangle and parallelogram area, then correct mistakes and explain one in a short paragraph.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on triangle area including finding missing dimensions.

objectives: Find area of trapezoids and other polygons by decomposing
Solve real-world area problems

days.title: Decomposing polygons
days.work: Split a trapezoid, a kite and a pentagon into triangles and rectangles and find each area; compare two different decompositions.

days.title: Trapezoid strategies
days.work: Use two copies of a trapezoid to make a parallelogram and solve 8 trapezoid-area problems with your own reasoning.

days.title: Measure a room
days.work: Measure a room or yard at home, sketch it to scale on graph paper, and calculate its area in square feet.

days.title: Covering a surface
days.work: Determine how many 1 ft square tiles and how many boxes of tiles (10 per box) would cover the room you measured, including irregular parts.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a 6-problem composite-figure assessment and present your floor plan calculation to a family member.

weeks.assessment: Composite polygon quiz plus floor-plan area project.

weeks.topic: Nets, surface area, squares and cubes
objectives: Draw nets of prisms and pyramids
Calculate surface area
Write s^2 and s^3 with exponents

days.title: Polyhedra and faces
days.work: Sort household objects into prisms and pyramids, count faces, edges and vertices, and record them in a table.

days.title: Unfold a box
days.work: Cut open a cereal box along its edges to make a net, measure each face and compute its surface area; compare with a partner's or parent's estimate.

days.title: Nets to surface area
days.work: Draw nets for a cube, a rectangular prism and a square pyramid on grid paper, fold one from cardstock, and calculate surface area of each.

days.title: Squares and cubes
days.work: Build cubes with snap cubes to model 2^3, 3^3, 4^3; write area of a square as s^2, volume of a cube as s^3, and surface area as 6s^2; evaluate for 8 side lengths.

days.title: Unit 1 test
days.work: Take the Unit 1 assessment (area of polygons, nets, surface area, exponent notation) and redo two missed problems with explanation.

objectives: Use ratio language a:b, a to b, a for every b
Represent ratios with diagrams

days.title: Introducing ratios
days.work: Describe collections of beans or counters with ratio language in three forms (3:2, 3 to 2, 3 for every 2) and write 10 ratio sentences.

days.title: Ratio diagrams
days.work: Draw discrete diagrams for recipe ratios (e.g., 2 cups flour for every 3 eggs) and answer which-ratio-matches questions.

days.title: Recipes and batches
days.work: Make one batch and a double batch of a drink mix (e.g., 2 scoops per 1 cup water), taste-test that they match, and explain why the ratio is equivalent.

days.title: Color mixing
days.work: Mix food coloring drops with water in 1:5 and 2:10 ratios to check that equivalent ratios make the same color; record observations in a table.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz: write and interpret ratios from pictures and stories; explain the difference between a part-to-part and part-to-whole ratio.

weeks.assessment: Ratio language quiz and color-mixing lab write-up.

weeks.topic: Equivalent ratios and double number lines
objectives: Generate equivalent ratios by multiplying or dividing
Use double number lines to solve problems

days.title: Defining equivalent ratios
days.work: Generate five ratios equivalent to 3:4 by multiplying both quantities, then decide whether 6 lists of ratio pairs are equivalent.

days.title: Double number lines
days.work: Draw double number lines for a 2-mile per 30-minute walking pace and answer 6 questions about time and distance.

days.title: Price per item
days.work: Use real grocery receipts to build double number lines for cost and quantity and find the cost of 1, 5 and 12 items.

days.title: Same speed?
days.work: Time yourself walking 20 steps, then use a double number line to predict time for 60 and 100 steps; test one prediction.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a quiz on equivalent ratios and double number lines; correct errors in a different color.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on equivalent ratios and double number lines.

objectives: Organize ratios in tables
Graph ratio pairs on the coordinate plane
Compare ratios

days.title: Ratio tables
days.work: Convert three double number lines into ratio tables, and fill in missing values in 8 tables using multiplication and scaling.

days.title: Tables and graphs
days.work: Plot ratio-table pairs (e.g., cups of rice to cups of water) on the first quadrant and notice that the points line up through (0,0).

days.title: Which is faster?
days.work: Compare two runners and two recipes using tables with a common row; justify which is faster or stronger in writing.

days.title: Problem solving
days.work: Solve 6 multi-step ratio word problems from Illustrative Math Grade 6 Unit 2, showing a table for each.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on completing tables, graphing ratio pairs and comparing ratios.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on ratio tables and graphs.

objectives: Use tape diagrams for part-part-whole problems
Choose an efficient representation

days.title: Tape diagrams
days.work: Use tape diagrams to solve 'ratio of boys to girls is 2:3 and there are 30 students' style problems (8 problems).

days.title: Trail mix lab
days.work: Make trail mix in a 3:2 nuts-to-raisins ratio for a total of 2 cups, using a tape diagram to plan amounts before measuring.

days.title: Choosing representations
days.work: Solve the same 4 problems with a table, a double number line and a tape diagram, and write which was most efficient and why.

days.title: Unit review
days.work: Complete a mixed ratio review set covering language, equivalence, tables, graphs and tape diagrams.

days.title: Unit 2 test
days.work: Take the Unit 2 end-of-unit assessment and write a reflection on the strategy you rely on most.

weeks.topic: Units of measure and unit rates
objectives: Convert measurement units using ratios
Find and interpret both unit rates in a ratio
materials: measuring cups and a liter bottle

days.title: Measuring with different units
days.work: Measure the same objects in inches and centimeters and in cups and milliliters, and record why the numbers differ.

days.title: Converting units
days.work: Use the ratio 1 in : 2.54 cm and 1 ft : 12 in to convert 12 measurements with ratio tables.

days.title: Two unit rates
days.work: For 'every 4 cups of water makes 3 servings' find both unit rates (cups per serving, servings per cup) and explain when each is useful.

days.title: Rates at home
days.work: Time how many seconds it takes to fill a 1-liter bottle at the faucet and calculate liters per minute and minutes per liter.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on unit conversion and finding unit rates.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on conversions and unit rates.

objectives: Solve constant speed problems
Compare unit prices to find the better buy
materials: store flyer or online grocery prices

days.title: Constant speed
days.work: Solve 8 problems using distance = rate x time reasoning with tables (e.g., a cyclist at 12 miles per hour).

days.title: Speed lab
days.work: Measure a 20-meter course, time yourself walking, jogging and hopping, and compute meters per second for each.

days.title: Unit price
days.work: Compare 6 pairs of grocery items in different sizes using unit price, and decide the better buy for each.

days.title: Rate problems
days.work: Solve mixed rate problems (pages per minute, heartbeats per minute, cost per ounce) and justify one answer to a family member.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on constant speed and unit price problems.

weeks.assessment: Quiz plus speed lab data table.

objectives: Understand percent as a rate per 100
Find percents of quantities using double number lines and tables

days.title: What is a percent?
days.work: Shade 10 x 10 grids to show 25%, 40%, 7% and 120%, and connect percents to fractions and decimals out of 100.

days.title: Benchmark percents
days.work: Find 10%, 25%, 50% and 75% of 8 different quantities using mental math and double number lines.

days.title: Percent of a quantity
days.work: Use tables to find percents such as 35% of $80 and 15% of 60 minutes (10 problems).

days.title: Sales and tips
days.work: Calculate sale prices from real ads (20% off, 30% off) and a 15% tip on three restaurant bills.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on percent meaning and finding a percent of a quantity.

weeks.topic: Finding the whole and percent problems
objectives: Find the whole given a part and percent
Find what percent one quantity is of another

days.title: Finding the whole
days.work: Solve problems like '12 is 30% of what number?' with tape diagrams and tables (10 problems).

days.title: What percent?
days.work: Find what percent one quantity is of another using nutrition labels (e.g., grams of sugar out of total carbohydrates).

days.title: Battery and progress bars
days.work: Use a device battery percentage and download bars to solve find-the-part, find-the-percent and find-the-whole problems.

days.title: Unit review
days.work: Complete a mixed review of unit rates, conversions, speed and percents.

days.title: Unit 3 test
days.work: Take the Unit 3 end-of-unit assessment and correct missed problems.

objectives: Interpret division as 'how many groups' or 'how much in each group'
Relate multiplication and division equations

days.title: Size of divisor and quotient
days.work: Predict and then compute what happens to quotients like 12 / 6, 12 / 1, 12 / 1/2, and write a rule about divisors less than 1.

days.title: Two meanings
days.work: Write two different story problems for 6 / 2 (how many groups vs. how much per group) and draw a diagram for each.

days.title: How many groups?
days.work: Use measuring cups to find how many 1/4 cups fit in 3 cups and how many 3/4 cups fit in 3 cups; record as division equations.

days.title: Using diagrams
days.work: Draw tape diagrams to solve 8 'how many groups' fraction problems, including answers that are not whole numbers.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz: match equations, diagrams and stories for fraction division.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on interpreting division and fraction diagrams.

objectives: Divide fractions using diagrams and the reciprocal
Explain why multiplying by the reciprocal works

days.title: How much in each group?
days.work: Solve problems like '3/4 of a pound fills 1/2 a bag; how much fills a whole bag?' with tape diagrams (6 problems).

days.title: Dividing by unit fractions
days.work: Notice that dividing by 1/3 is the same as multiplying by 3, and test the pattern with 10 examples.

days.title: Algorithm for fraction division
days.work: Use the reciprocal method to compute 15 quotients including mixed numbers, and check each with multiplication.

days.title: Explain it
days.work: Write a short explanation, with a diagram, of why 2/3 / 1/6 = 4, and critique a sample student's incorrect solution.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on computing fraction quotients and explaining the algorithm.

weeks.assessment: Fraction division computation quiz with one written explanation.

objectives: Solve multi-step fraction division word problems
Use division to find lengths and areas

days.title: Fractional lengths
days.work: Measure a ribbon and find how many 3/8-yard pieces can be cut from 4 1/2 yards; solve 6 similar length problems.

days.title: Rectangles with fractional sides
days.work: Find a missing side when area and one side are fractions (e.g., area 2 1/2 sq ft, width 3/4 ft).

days.title: Recipes
days.work: Scale a recipe calling for 2/3 cup sugar to fit a 1/2-cup measuring scoop and solve 5 recipe-division problems.

days.title: Write your own
days.work: Write and solve three fraction-division story problems and trade with a family member to solve.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on fraction word problems.

objectives: Find volume of prisms with fractional edges
Show V = lwh by packing unit cubes of fractional size

days.title: Packing cubes
days.work: Pack a small box with 1/2-inch cubes, count them, and show that the count x 1/8 cubic inch equals l x w x h.

days.title: Volume formulas
days.work: Compute volumes of 10 prisms with fractional edges using V = lwh and V = Bh.

days.title: Missing dimensions
days.work: Use fraction division to find a missing edge when volume and two edges are known (6 problems).

days.title: Unit review
days.work: Mixed review of fraction division and volume, including one aquarium or garden-bed design problem.

days.title: Unit 4 test
days.work: Take the Unit 4 assessment and reflect on the meaning of division.

objectives: Add and subtract decimals fluently
Multiply decimals and explain decimal placement

days.title: Decimals in money
days.work: Add and subtract prices from a shopping list, lining up place values, and find change from $50.

days.title: Adding and subtracting decimals
days.work: Solve 20 decimal sums and differences with up to thousandths, including regrouping across zeros.

days.title: Multiplying decimals
days.work: Use area diagrams and fractions (0.3 x 0.4 = 3/10 x 4/10) to explain decimal placement, then compute 12 products.

days.title: Decimal applications
days.work: Calculate total cost of buying fabric at $4.75 per yard for 2.5 yards and 5 similar problems.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on decimal addition, subtraction and multiplication.

objectives: Divide multi-digit whole numbers with the standard algorithm
Divide decimals

days.title: Partial quotients
days.work: Divide 3- and 4-digit numbers by 2-digit divisors using partial quotients, then compare to the standard algorithm.

days.title: Long division
days.work: Complete 12 long-division problems with the standard algorithm, checking each by multiplication.

days.title: Dividing decimals
days.work: Divide decimals by whole numbers and by decimals by multiplying both numbers by powers of 10 (12 problems).

days.title: Decimal word problems
days.work: Solve problems such as splitting a $47.85 bill among 3 people and finding miles per gallon.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Semester 1 cumulative review quiz covering area, ratios, percents, fraction division and decimals.

weeks.topic: Factors, multiples and the distributive property
objectives: Find GCF and LCM
Factor sums with the distributive property

days.title: Greatest common factor
days.work: Find the largest square tile that exactly covers a 24 x 36 rectangle, then find GCF for 10 pairs of numbers.

days.title: Least common multiple
days.work: Solve 'hot dogs come in 10s, buns in 8s' problems and find LCM for 10 pairs.

days.title: GCF or LCM?
days.work: Sort 8 word problems as GCF or LCM situations and solve each.

days.title: Distributive property
days.work: Rewrite sums like 36 + 8 as 4(9 + 2) using the GCF and use area models to show why it works.

days.title: Unit 5 test
days.work: Take the Unit 5 assessment on decimals, long division, GCF/LCM.

objectives: Write expressions with variables from words
Identify parts of an expression

days.title: Letters for numbers
days.work: Write expressions for situations such as 'x more than 5' and 'a number divided by 3'; translate 15 phrases into expressions.

days.title: Parts of expressions
days.work: Label terms, coefficients and constants in 10 expressions and describe 2(x + 5) as 'a product of two factors'.

days.title: Expression match
days.work: Play a card-matching game linking verbal descriptions, expressions and tape diagrams.

days.title: Evaluating expressions
days.work: Evaluate 12 expressions for given variable values, e.g., 3x + 4 when x = 2.5.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on writing, reading and evaluating expressions.

objectives: Understand a solution makes an equation true
Solve x + p = q and px = q
materials: balance scale or hanger diagram printouts

days.title: True or false?
days.work: Test whether given values make 10 equations true using substitution.

days.title: Hanger diagrams
days.work: Use hanger diagrams (or a homemade coat-hanger balance with paper clips) to model and solve equations like x + 3 = 7 and 3x = 12.

days.title: Solving addition equations
days.work: Solve 12 equations of the form x + p = q with fractions and decimals, checking by substitution.

days.title: Solving multiplication equations
days.work: Solve 12 equations of the form px = q, including 2/3 x = 10, and write stories for two of them.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on solving one-step equations and writing equations for word problems.

objectives: Use properties to write equivalent expressions
Combine like terms

days.title: Same value, different form
days.work: Substitute several values into pairs like 3(x + 2) and 3x + 6 to test equivalence, recording results in a table.

days.title: Distributive property with variables
days.work: Use area diagrams to expand 4(x + 3) and factor 6x + 18 (12 problems).

days.title: Combining like terms
days.work: Use paper algebra tiles to simplify expressions like 2x + 5 + 3x + 1 and explain why x + x is 2x.

days.title: Prove or disprove
days.work: Decide whether 8 pairs of expressions are equivalent and justify with properties or a counterexample.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on generating and identifying equivalent expressions.

objectives: Evaluate expressions with whole-number exponents
Use order of operations including exponents
Evaluate formulas

days.title: Paper-folding powers
days.work: Fold a sheet of paper in half repeatedly, record layers as 2^1, 2^2 ... and predict layers after 10 folds.

days.title: Evaluating powers
days.work: Evaluate 15 expressions such as 3^4, (1/2)^3 and 0.2^2 and compare 2^5 with 5^2.

days.title: Order of operations
days.work: Evaluate 15 expressions like 2 + 3 x 4^2 and (2 + 3)^2 and find the errors in three worked examples.

days.title: Formulas
days.work: Evaluate V = s^3, SA = 6s^2 and A = 1/2 bh for given values, and choose a formula to solve a packaging problem.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on exponents, order of operations and formulas.

weeks.assessment: Exponent and order of operations quiz.

objectives: Identify independent and dependent variables
Represent a relationship with a table, graph and equation

days.title: Two changing quantities
days.work: For situations like 'earning $9 per hour', name the independent and dependent variables and write an equation d = 9h.

days.title: Tables to graphs
days.work: Make tables and first-quadrant graphs for three equations (y = 4x, y = x + 3, y = 2.5x) and compare their shapes.

days.title: Real data
days.work: Fill a cup with water a few tablespoons at a time and weigh it, then make a table, graph and equation for the relationship.

days.title: Unit review
days.work: Mixed review of expressions, equations, exponents and variable relationships.

days.title: Unit 6 test
days.work: Take the Unit 6 end-of-unit assessment and correct errors.

objectives: Use signed numbers in context
Locate rational numbers and opposites on the number line

days.title: Temperature and elevation
days.work: Record temperatures in different places (e.g., Death Valley highs, Lake Tahoe winter lows) and elevations above and below sea level, and explain the meaning of 0.

days.title: Opposites
days.work: Mark 12 numbers and their opposites on a number line, including -2.5 and 3/4, and explain why -(-4) = 4.

days.title: Money and signed numbers
days.work: Represent deposits, withdrawals and debt with positive and negative numbers in 8 situations.

days.title: Rational numbers on the line
days.work: Place fractions and decimals between -3 and 3 on a carefully scaled number line.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on signed numbers in context and number-line placement.

objectives: Order rational numbers
Interpret absolute value as distance from zero

days.title: Comparing signed numbers
days.work: Write inequality statements comparing pairs like -7 and -3, and explain them as positions on a number line.

days.title: Ordering
days.work: Order sets of rational numbers from least to greatest using a card sort, including fractions and decimals.

days.title: Absolute value
days.work: Find |x| for 12 numbers and interpret absolute value as distance, e.g., a debt of $30 means balance -30.

days.title: Comparing statements
days.work: Distinguish statements about order and about absolute value (e.g., -24 < -14 but |-24| > |-14|) in 8 contexts.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on ordering and absolute value.

objectives: Write inequalities for real constraints
Graph solutions on a number line

days.title: Writing inequalities
days.work: Write inequalities for constraints like 'you must be at least 48 inches to ride' and 'fewer than 30 students' (10 situations).

days.title: Graphing solutions
days.work: Graph x > c, x < c, x >= c and x <= c on number lines and test values with substitution.

days.title: Infinitely many solutions
days.work: Explain why x > 3 has infinitely many solutions and identify whether given values are solutions.

days.title: Inequalities in context
days.work: Solve real problems like saving at least $120 and decide which values make sense in context (whole people, decimals of money).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on writing, graphing and interpreting inequalities.

objectives: Plot points in all four quadrants
Find distances between points with a common coordinate

days.title: Four quadrants
days.work: Plot 20 points including negative and fractional coordinates and name each point's quadrant.

days.title: Reflections
days.work: Reflect points over each axis and describe how the signs of the coordinates change.

days.title: Distances
days.work: Find distances between points like (-3, 4) and (5, 4) using absolute value, in 10 problems.

days.title: Coordinate map
days.work: Draw a neighborhood map on a coordinate grid with home at the origin and solve walking-distance problems along the streets.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on plotting, reflecting and distance.

weeks.assessment: Coordinate plane quiz and map project.

objectives: Draw polygons from vertices
Find side lengths, perimeter and area using coordinates

days.title: Drawing polygons
days.work: Plot and connect vertices to draw rectangles, triangles and trapezoids in all four quadrants.

days.title: Side lengths
days.work: Use coordinates to find horizontal and vertical side lengths and perimeters of 8 polygons.

days.title: Area on the grid
days.work: Find areas of coordinate polygons by decomposing or enclosing in rectangles.

days.title: Design challenge
days.work: Design a garden plot with 4-6 vertices on Desmos having area exactly 48 square units and list its coordinates.

days.title: Unit 7 test
days.work: Take the Unit 7 end-of-unit assessment on rational numbers, inequalities and the coordinate plane.

objectives: Recognize statistical questions
Make and describe dot plots

days.title: Statistical questions
days.work: Sort 12 questions as statistical or not (e.g., 'How old am I?' vs 'How old are students at my co-op?') and write 3 of your own.

days.title: Collect data
days.work: Survey 20 or more people (family, friends, co-op) with your statistical question and record results in a frequency table.

days.title: Dot plots
days.work: Make a dot plot of your survey data and of a provided data set on daily screen time.

days.title: Describing distributions
days.work: Describe the center, spread and shape (symmetric, skewed, clusters, gaps) of three dot plots in writing.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on statistical questions and dot plots.

objectives: Organize data into bins
Make and interpret histograms

days.title: Reaction time data
days.work: Measure reaction time 25 times with the ruler-drop test and record the catch distance in centimeters.

days.title: Making histograms
days.work: Group your reaction data into equal bins and draw a histogram with labeled axes.

days.title: Dot plot or histogram?
days.work: Compare a dot plot and histogram of the same data and write when each display is more useful.

days.title: Interpreting histograms
days.work: Answer questions about histograms of California city temperatures and dog weights, describing shape and spread.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on building and reading histograms.

objectives: Understand mean as fair share and balance point
Calculate and interpret MAD

days.title: Fair share
days.work: Use stacks of snap cubes to level out unequal towers and connect the result to adding and dividing.

days.title: Balance point
days.work: Show on a dot plot that the mean is the point where distances above and below balance, using 4 small data sets.

days.title: Mean absolute deviation
days.work: Compute the MAD for two basketball players' points per game and decide who is more consistent.

days.title: Comparing groups
days.work: Compare two data sets (e.g., plant heights with and without fertilizer) using mean and MAD.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on mean and MAD.

objectives: Find median and quartiles
Make box plots and interpret IQR

days.title: Median
days.work: Line up 11 index cards of data to find the median and see why it resists outliers compared with the mean.

days.title: Five-number summary
days.work: Find minimum, Q1, median, Q3 and maximum for 6 data sets and compute range and IQR.

days.title: Box plots
days.work: Draw box plots for your reaction-time data and a family height data set.

days.title: Comparing box plots
days.work: Compare two box plots (e.g., Los Angeles vs San Francisco monthly temperatures) and write 3 conclusions.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on median, IQR and box plots.

objectives: Choose appropriate measures of center and spread
Carry out a statistical investigation

days.title: Mean or median?
days.work: Decide for 6 data sets whether mean/MAD or median/IQR better describes them, based on shape and outliers.

days.title: Plan an investigation
days.work: Write a statistical question, plan how to collect at least 30 data points, and begin collecting.

days.title: Analyze
days.work: Display your data with two plot types and calculate center and spread measures.

days.title: Present
days.work: Create a poster or slides answering your question with data, and present it to your family.

days.title: Unit 8 test
days.work: Take the Unit 8 end-of-unit assessment on data and distributions.

weeks.assessment: Unit 8 assessment and statistics project rubric.

objectives: Apply ratios, percents and decimals to a real plan
Communicate a mathematical model

days.title: Choose a destination
days.work: Pick a California destination, find the distance, and use a car's miles-per-gallon rate to calculate fuel needed.

days.title: Budget
days.work: Build a budget with lodging, food and tickets, compute totals with decimals and add 8% sales tax.

days.title: Time and speed
days.work: Use average speed to plan driving time and a schedule of stops.

days.title: Packing volume
days.work: Determine whether your luggage (measure boxes or bags) fits a car trunk of given volume, using fractional dimensions.

days.title: Present the plan
days.work: Present your trip plan with all calculations and answer family questions about your choices.

objectives: Review all grade 6 standards
Demonstrate mastery on a final assessment

days.title: Review: ratios and number
days.work: Complete a review set on ratios, percents, fraction division and decimals; star problems to revisit.

days.title: Review: expressions and geometry
days.work: Complete a review set on equations, expressions, area, surface area and volume.

days.title: Review: rational numbers and data
days.work: Complete a review set on negatives, the coordinate plane and statistics; then take the Khan Academy 6th grade course challenge.

days.title: Final exam
days.work: Take a 40-problem cumulative final assessment covering all grade 6 domains.

days.title: Reflection and goals
days.work: Correct the final, write a reflection on your growth this year, and set goals for Math 7.
